q-144070.name: Question 1
q-144070.problem: Suppose we want to measure the area of the school playground. What units could we use?
q-144070.worked_solution: We can measure length in meters $(\text{m}).$ When measuring lengths in meters, areas are measured in $\text{m}\times \text{m},$ which is usually written as ${\text{m}}^{2}.$

q-144168.name: Question 3
q-144168.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14153327/assets/171e55cb16b67bba62ca0a1e85c54ca2cb8fc10e8284b9ca7fdcf9ddd3862502.png)

What is the area of the square above?
q-144168.worked_solution:
To calculate the area $A$ of a square, we square its side length. Therefore, the area of the square is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =(2\,\text{m})^{2} \\  & =2\,\text{m}\times 2\,\text{m} \\  & =(2\times 2)\times (\text{m}\times \text{m}) \\  & =4\,{\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-144197.name: Question 5
q-144197.problem: A cube has a side length of $8\,\text{m}.$ What is the volume of the cube?
q-144197.worked_solution:
To find the volume $V$ of a cube, we cube its side length. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =(8\,\text{m})^{3} \\  & =8\,\text{m}\times 8\,\text{m}\times 8\,\text{m} \\  & =(8\times 8\times 8)\times (\text{m}\times \text{m}\times \text{m}) \\  & =512\,{\text{m}}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-144197.html:
Question 5
?

A cube has a side length of 8m. What is the volume of the cube?

a
512m
b
512m3
c
512m2
d
192m2
e
192m3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the volume V of a cube, we cube its side length. Therefore, V=(8m)3=8m×8m×8m=(8×8×8)×(m×m×m)=512m3.
q-144197.knowledge_point: Computing a Volume With the Correct Units

q-144196.name: Question 6
q-144196.problem: A cube has a side length of $9\,\text{mm}.$ What is the volume of the cube?
q-144196.worked_solution:
To find the volume $V$ of a cube, we cube its side length. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =(9\,\text{mm})^{3} \\  & =9\,\text{mm}\times 9\,\text{mm}\times 9\,\text{mm} \\  & =(9\times 9\times 9)\times (\text{mm}\times \text{mm}\times \text{mm}) \\  & =729\,{\text{mm}}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
